## What and why

Step 03 implemented the `create-engine-skeleton` feature's bounded recipe route.
It separates pipdata release coordination from calculation and makes stamp the
only selector for that route. It does not replace the legacy manifest-driven
route when `recipes` is omitted.

**Owner:** pipdata owns release coordination; stamp owns rebuild decisions and
pipload owns the access adapter. **Recorder:** The pipdata Code session recorded
the October 27 package work and its checks. This page is a pipsystem backfill.

## Inputs and outputs

**Inputs:** The documented `pipdata::pd_run_pipeline()` recipe route accepts a
`TEST` release context with an initialized local stamp root and an explicit
node list. Nodes provide paths, parent pins, a calculation, known helpers and
constants, semantic metadata, and an `rds`, `qs2`, or `fst` format. The original
contract required the approved Windows E-drive runtime; it was incremental only
and rejected nondefault legacy controls.

**Outputs:** A `data.table` with preview decision, outcome, reason, exact
version and proof IDs, and whether work was attempted. The route delegates
selection and revalidation to public stamp functions and permits exact pinned
reads through the approved adapter. It does not produce a registered test
release by itself.

## Verification and gaps

**2026-11-25 pinned-record check: PASS.** The delivered public manual matches
the M2 plan's authority boundary on the opt-in recipe route: stamp selects and
revalidates run/skip/blocked work, and legacy manifests do not select for that
route. The same manual distinguishes the separate legacy behavior. The delivered
pin is present in the current local branch history. Neither the documentation
comparison nor that ancestry check runs the engine or proves deployment.

**Historical fixture integration:** The October 27 handoff reports a selected
41-test, 286-expectation gate and a separate installed built/skipped/empty smoke
with exact data and metadata reads. It records stamp `0.0.11` content
`5d1ddebdc926dad9c6ec99c08a65e74baee0da92` and pipload `1.0.0` adapter commit
`4ef0d90a974cb6ff0725da69373bde421dd04ad5` as the producers used. The tested
pipdata candidate was uncommitted; `8cde5c5efd4ab87f419661221f202205e5e87214`
is the cited delivery revision (version `1.0.0`), not the build SHA for that
run. The October 28 work report supersedes the initial count with 46 tests and
324 expectations, no failures/errors/warnings/skips, and a fresh installed
smoke on `rds`, `qs2`, and `fst`. The corrected run identifies its uncommitted
candidate by a 182-file source manifest on base
`4728a2b2d2aadb43ce72ddf6c19732f75188a208` (work report lines 403-415),
not by the delivery SHA. Forty-one existing test files remained excluded.

**Current runtime and live testing: NOT RUN.** No R package was loaded (loaded
version and build SHA `UNKNOWN`). No local substitute for the original isolated
Windows runtime was verified, and no pipeline entry point, live DLW, mounted
storage, or release target was used. The registered pipdata checkout was clean
(no staged, unstaged, or untracked paths) on `fix/m2-cpi-admission-checkpoint` at
`c70ae403acde648aff1a49d8d3178ca0202c6064`. Pipload was cited through the
handoff; its checkout was not read.

**Gaps:** The selected package integration does not certify the umbrella Plan's
L-authority/V6 gate (work report lines 338-344). It does not establish default-branch
adapter installation, full-suite or shared-storage/concurrency behavior, or the
complete survey-to-release chain. The handoff and work report provide historical
fixture results, not tests re-executed against the current checkout.
